key_decisions.decision: Retains both similar Azariah names and the source's title Israel.
Makes consolidation and fratricide explicit without excusing the violence.
Preserves the covenant and lamp image rather than reducing them to succession.
Retains difficult final object without inserting an escape or victory claim.
Retains prostitution as the source's sharp religious image, explained in vocabulary.
Preserves Elijah's letter and the two named standards without chronology repair.
Keeps divine accusation, religious metaphor, and explicit comparison with murdered brothers.
Retains bodily horror and duration rather than euphemizing the judgment.
Retains Jehoahaz here and the captivity language without importing later deaths.
Retains two years and distinguishes funeral burning from cremation.
Repeats source figures and preserves the stark unregretted departure and burial exclusion.
